title: How to Automate Invoice Downloads from Vendor Portals
summary: Automate invoice downloads from vendor portals with Skyvern. Set up logins, collect invoice PDFs, save files to cloud storage, and schedule monthly runs.
body_markdown:
Some vendors email their invoices. Others leave them in a billing portal for you to collect every month. If you manage dozens of those accounts, fetching the PDFs becomes a job of its own.


And that's the exact use-case we've built Skyvern for (I'm Skyvern's CEO).


You can[automate invoice downloads with Skyvern](https://www.skyvern.com/use-cases) by describing the task, connecting the vendor login, and scheduling the resulting workflow.


In this article, I'll walk you though how to setup invoice downloads from a vendor portal and show you how to automate the monthly collection.


*If you'd rather skip the explanations and try it yourself, you can*[try Skyvern for free](https://www.skyvern.com/pricing) *with enough credits to setup your first few workflows.*


## Before you start


We'll setup invoice collection from one vendor portals so at the very least you’ll need:


- **A Skyvern account** to build and run the workflow.
- **The vendor’s login URL and credentials** , with permission to view and download invoices.
- **Access to any two-factor authentication** the portal requires, such as an authenticator app, email inbox, or SMS number.
- **A month of invoices you’ve already collected** to check whether the first automated run downloads the right files.


You can retrieve the PDFs directly from Skyvern after a run. If you want automatic uploads to cloud storage, also have your destination’s connection details and credentials ready.


## 1. Connect the vendor account


Open **Credentials → Add → Password** in Skyvern. Enter the portal's login URL, username, and password, and give the credential a name you'll recognize, such as “Acme billing.”


If the account uses[two-factor authentication](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/how-skyvern-handles-authentication/) , expand that part of the form:


- For an authenticator app, save the authenticator key so Skyvern can generate codes.
- For email codes, connect the receiving inbox or arrange to forward the codes to Skyvern.
- For SMS codes, supply them through the app or API. An unattended run needs an automated way to deliver those messages.


The[credentials guide](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/credentials) covers each option.


The Add Credential form in Skyvern.


## 2. Tell Skyvern which invoices to collect


On Skyvern's Home page, send[Automation Copilot](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/launch-week-day-1-automation-copilot-faster-time-to-automation/) a description of the task. Be specific about the billing account and date range, particularly when one login gives you access to several companies.


Here's a prompt you can adapt:


```text
Build an agent to collect invoice PDFs from [vendor portal URL].
Use the saved login I select.


Create inputs for billing_account, start_date, and end_date.
Open the selected billing account and find invoices issued between
those dates, including both dates.


Check every results page and download each matching invoice's
original PDF. Exclude receipts and account statements.


Return a list with the invoice number, issue date, and downloaded
filename. Report failed downloads and say if no invoices match.
```


Making the account and dates inputs lets you change them when you run the agent. You won't need to edit the instructions each month.


Copilot opens Studio and builds the workflow. Review its proposed changes before clicking **Accept** . The[Copilot quickstart](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/quickstart) shows how proposals and test results appear.


Read the generated steps for anything specific to your vendor. A portal might call invoices “billing documents,” hide older files behind an archive tab, or show payment dates beside issue dates. Tell Copilot about those details so it uses the right route and filters.


## 3. Test a complete month


Pick a month whose invoices you already have. Click **Run** , enter the account and dates, and watch the agent work through the portal.


For a portal with individual download buttons, the workflow needs to repeat the download action for each invoice. Skyvern's **File Download** block provides instructions in **Download Goal** and a waiting period in **Download Timeout** . The timeout is useful when the portal takes a while to generate a PDF. See the[block reference](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/reference/blocks#file-download) for these settings.


The File Download block


When the run finishes, retrieve the PDFs from **Run → Outputs → Downloaded files** . Compare their invoice numbers with your existing set and open a sample to confirm the company and dates. This catches problems a file count alone would miss, such as downloading the same invoice twice.


If something is missing, use the recording to locate the problem. For example, if the agent stops after the first page, ask Copilot to add pagination. If it clicks Download before a report is ready, adjust the waiting step. Run outputs and recordings are described in the[run guide](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/runs) .


## 4. Choose where the files go


For an occasional collection, downloading the files from the run may be enough. For a recurring process, add a step that sends them to your team's storage.


If you use Amazon S3, add **Cloud Storage Upload** after the download steps. Select S3, configure the bucket, region, and credentials, and set a folder path such as` invoices/acme/` . The same block also supports Azure Blob Storage. Configuration details are in the[storage block documentation](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/reference/blocks#cloud-storage-upload) .


The download block's **File Name** setting lets you replace a generic name like` invoice.pdf` . Use fields captured from the portal to produce a recognizable filename:


```text
acme_INV-10482_2026-09-12.pdf
```


Before scheduling, decide how to handle invoices you've already collected. Keep a record of the vendor account and invoice number, then add a lookup in the workflow or receiving system before saving another copy. That gives a retry a way to skip invoices already saved.


## 5. Set up the monthly run


A recurring workflow needs a changing date range. Ask Copilot to add a step that calculates the previous calendar month's start and end dates each time the agent runs. Test the calculation across a month boundary: an October run should request September invoices, while a November run should request October invoices.


Then open **Schedule** in Studio. Choose **Monthly** , set the day, time, and timezone, and review **Next Scheduled Runs** . Skyvern's[scheduling documentation](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/runs#schedule-an-agent) explains the controls.


Match the schedule to the vendor's billing cycle. If it normally posts the previous month's invoices by the third, a run on the fifth gives it time to finish. For vendors that post files late, consider collecting an overlapping date range and using your collection record to skip documents already received.


Run History shows previous runs and their outcomes. If[a browser automation run fails](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/error-handling-in-browser-automation/) , open it to find the failing block. **Fix with Copilot** passes the failure to Copilot so you can review a proposed correction.


## What's next


Congratulations! You automated your first invoice retrieval workflow with Skyvern.


Now you can reuse parts of that workflow to expand to other vendor portals!


It's easy: you just need to keep the parts that stay the same, such as the output fields, storage destination, and duplicate checks and give each portal its own login.


You can also implement advanced features like intelligent scheduling, priority-based processing, and integration with existing ERP systems. These enhancements change invoice processing from a manual bottleneck into a competitive advantage.


The scalability extends beyond just downloading invoices to complete[integration capabilities](https://www.skyvern.com/integrations) that connect with your broader business processes.
